correctness.rationale: The hypergeometric formula for \(R_m\) is derived from species-absence probabilities. Two independent complete generators agree on every positive abundance multiset through \(N=10\), and all same-\((N,S)\) unordered pairs are compared at every interior \(m\) using exact rational arithmetic. The exhaustive check gives no strict crossing for \(N\le9\), exactly one at \(N=10\), and reproduces all stated witness fractions and endpoint identities.

value.rationale: Individual-based rarefaction is used specifically to compare richness at standardized sampling effort, and crossing curves make such comparisons sample-size dependent. Fixing both total abundance and observed richness isolates this effect within a natural ecological feasible set. The theorem gives the smallest possible exact reversal and a transparent mechanism: finite-sample pair concentration controls the early curve, whereas singleton count controls the near-census endpoint.
